On November 6, 2026, the Indian Rupee staged an aggressive recovery, closing at a 6-month high of 93.91 against the US Dollar as Brent crude softened under $94 a barrel. While mainstream financial news treated this as a routine market fluctuation, the underlying mechanics reveal an institutional masterclass by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Behind the scenes, the central bank deployed its active dollar buffer and strategic forex interventions across spot and non-deliverable forward (NDF) desks to neutralize speculative short attacks.
